title: Blink — Spend Crypto Like Cash
description: Pitch deck for Blink, a mobile application that enables users spend crypto like cash and merchants to accept crypto payments via Bluetooth and receive instant settlement in their local currency.

slides.title: SPEND CRYPTO LIKE CASH.
slides.subtitle: Blink is a mobile application that enables users spend crypto like cash and merchants to accept crypto payments via Bluetooth and receive instant settlement in their local currency.

columns.title: USERS
points: No seamless way to spend crypto at checkout — holders are stuck converting before they can pay.
P2P conversion carries real fraud risk. Binance estimates P2P scam losses reached $3B in 2025.
Very few real-world places actually accept crypto payment today.

columns.title: MERCHANTS
points: Most merchants avoid crypto entirely — the integration feels too complex.
Price volatility between sale and settlement is a real, unmanaged risk.
No accessible infrastructure exists for blockchain-powered commerce at the till.

grid.question: Who it affects
grid.answer:
Users can't spend USDC day-to-day without routing through P2P first.

Merchants lose customers because accepting crypto today feels risky.

grid.question: Why people should care
grid.answer: Millions of crypto holders across Africa want to spend, not just hold. Today's tooling blocks real financial inclusion at the exact moment it's needed most.

grid.question: Why now
grid.answer: Over 54 million Africans use crypto today. The region processed $200B+ in crypto transactions in 2025 driven by need, not hype.

columns.title: FOR USERS
points: Spend crypto instantly in real-world transactions, over Bluetooth.
Zero technical knowledge required. Pay the way you already pay with cash.

columns.title: FOR MERCHANTS
points: Accept crypto with zero volatility exposure — settlement lands in local currency.
Instant settlement at the point of sale, no waiting on confirmations.
Accept payment via Bluetooth, QR code, or the Blink Crypto POS.

slides.title:
EVERY DIGITAL ASSET
SHOULD BE SPENDABLE
EVERYWHERE.

DIGITAL COMMERCE IS
ENTERING A NEW ERA.

numbers.desc: Crypto inflow to Nigeria in a single year. Stablecoins drive ~60% of Sub-Saharan Africa's crypto activity.
Average cross-border remittance cost in Sub-Saharan Africa, among the highest globally.
Annual crypto transaction volume across Africa, with merchant acceptance still limited.
Of African businesses still lack blockchain-native payment infrastructure today.

slides.title:
SIZING THE
OPPORTUNITY.
slides.note: Africa is one of the world's fastest-growing crypto markets driven by remittances, everyday payments, and currency instability, not speculation.

flow.title: Transaction Fees
flow.desc: Charged per transaction processed through the network, scales directly with volume.

flow.title: FX / Settlement Margin
flow.desc: Captured on every conversion at the point of instant settlement into local currency.

phases.title: Merchant First
points: Onboard small merchants, retail shops, vendors
Focus on high-traffic areas

phases.title: User Activation
points: Target crypto-native users
Incentivize first transactions

phases.title: Network Effects
points: More merchants drive more users — and back again
Launch infrastructure products
Scale across Africa

slides.title:
EARLY. LIVE.
ALREADY GROWING.
slides.chartNote: +150% user growth in 2 months of operation — with $0 spent on marketing.

items.title: Enable Payments
items.outcome: Outcome: Make crypto spendable in everyday commerce.

items.title: Expand Commerce
items.desc: Extend Blink across online and offline businesses.
items.outcome: Outcome: Enable businesses to accept payments anywhere.

slides.title: $100K
slides.subtitle: Pre-seed capital to scale merchant acquisition, harden settlement infrastructure, and accelerate the path to network effects.

members.name: Ebube Ebuka Onuora
members.bio: Ebube is the rare founder who has sat on both sides of the problem he is solving. Nearly 5 years inside the Nigerian banking system gave him an intimate understanding of exactly how and where the system fails ordinary people, knowledge that no classroom or accelerator program can teach. He carried that frustration into software development, completing ALX SE program, Utiva Full Stack bootcamp and multiple blockchain programs before putting his skills to work through open source contributions on OnlyDust and Drips shipping real code in real Web3 projects long before Blink existed. That combination of financial sector experience and hands-on builder credibility is what earned him a $25,000 grant from the Starknet Foundation to build Fortichain and it is what makes him uniquely qualified to build the payment infrastructure Africa has always needed.

members.name: Eleazar Shekoaga Musa
members.bio: Eleazar Shekoaga Musa is a Software and Blockchain Engineer with 5 years experience and a strong background in backend systems, decentralized infrastructure, and scalable application architecture. He has experience building Web2 and Web3 solutions across fintech, and payment infrastructure, contributing to projects focused on transparency, accessibility, and open digital ecosystems. Eleazar has contributed to open-source projects within ecosystems, working on smart contract integrations, payment rails, wallet infrastructure, and developer tooling. He has contributed to open source projects such as Autoswapp and this reflects his focus on building interoperable systems that bridge traditional software engineering with decentralized technologies, he has developed and contributed to enterprise-grade applications including multi-chain wallets, blockchain payment SDKs, and public infrastructure solutions.

members.name: Jethro Adamu
members.bio: Jethro Adamu is a Fullstack, Mobile, and Blockchain Developer with 8 years of experience building scalable Web2 and Web3 applications across Europe, the United States, and Africa. He has contributed to globally used products, including leading development at EcoHotels, where he managed a cross-functional team building a sustainable hotel booking platform for international travelers which generated 300k EUR last year in revenue, processed 160k bookings in total. He also led the development team of Nextup and built high-performance microservices and mobile applications for Nextup, United States. In the Web3 and fintech space, he engineered AutoRamp at TheBuidl Grid, a B2B platform enabling seamless fiat on-ramping and off-ramping infrastructure and also build Runescard, a crypto giftcard platform and has processed 3k giftcards during 6 months of operations.

lines: Blink is building the infrastructure that connects them.

title: Faith in a Digital Age
description: Staying God-Centered in a Tech-Driven World

slides.title: FAITH IN A DIGITAL AGE
slides.subtitle: Staying God-Centered in a Tech-Driven World
slides.keyVerse: “And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.
slides.meta:
FAITH IN A DIGITAL AGE


Staying God-Centered in a Tech-Driven World
2026

slides.title: CONNECTED, YET DISTRACTED
points: We are the most connected generation in human history, yet paradoxically one of the most distracted, anxious, and spiritually fatigued.
Phones wake us up. Algorithms shape our opinions. Screens dominate our attention.
Yet the Bible says: “Be still, and know that I am God.” — Psalm 46:10
The central question is not: Is technology evil? But rather: How do we remain God-centered when technology competes for our attention, identity, and devotion?
Technology is not new. What is new is speed, scale, and intimacy—technology now lives with us, on us, and inside our thinking patterns.

grid.title: Speed Over Depth
points: Instant messages
Short videos
Rapid consumption
But spiritual growth requires time, patience, and silence

grid.title: Visibility Over Integrity
points: Likes, shares, followers
Online validation
God values who we are in secret, not what trends publicly. “Man looketh on the outward appearance, but the Lord looketh on the heart.” — 1 Samuel 16:7

grid.title: Information Without Transformation
points: Endless sermons, podcasts, devotionals
Yet little obedience or heart change
We know about God more than ever—but knowing God is different from consuming content about Him.

examples.verse: “Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself.
examples.lesson: God-centered faith starts with internal conviction, not external control.

examples.verse: “And he withdrew himself into the wilderness, and prayed.
examples.lesson: If Jesus needed silence, how much more do we in an age of constant notifications?

examples.verse: “Be not conformed to this world, but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind.
examples.lesson: The danger today is digital conformity—thinking, reacting, and valuing what algorithms reward.

threats.title: Digital Idolatry
points: Anything that commands our attention, shapes our identity, controls our emotions can become an idol.
Phones don’t bow to us—we bow to them.

threats.title: Fragmented Attention = Weakened Prayer
points: Prayer requires stillness, focus, presence.
But the digital world trains us to multitask, scroll, rush.
A distracted mind struggles to hear a still, small voice.

threats.title: Performance Christianity
points: Posting scriptures but lacking obedience
Public faith without private devotion
Jesus warned: “This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth… but their heart is far from me.” — Matthew 15:8

threats.title: Moral Desensitization
points: Constant exposure to pornography, violence, pride culture, mockery of holiness slowly dulls spiritual sensitivity.

slides.title: TECHNOLOGY IS NEUTRAL
slides.verse: “All things are lawful for me, but I will not be brought under the power of any.

ways.title: As a Tool
points: Learning
Evangelism
Community building

ways.title: As an Idol
points: Validation
Escape
Identity

ways.title: As an Assignment
points: Using digital spaces intentionally for God’s purposes
We don’t just consume technology—we design, shape, and govern it.

practices.title: Practice Digital Discernment
points: Ask regularly: Does this draw me closer to God or dull my spirit?
Does this control me or serve me?

practices.title: Establish Sacred Rhythms
points: Screen-free prayer time
Tech-free devotion moments
Intentional fasting from digital noise
What you don’t schedule, technology will replace.

practices.title: Be a Light in Digital Spaces
points: “Ye are the light of the world.” — Matthew 5:14
Integrity online, Truth without toxicity, Faith without performance

practices.title: Redefine Success
points: Not: Followers, Views, Virality
But: Obedience, Fruit, Faithfulness

slides.title: USING TECHNOLOGY FOR THE EXPANSION OF GOD'S KINGDOM
slides.keyVerse: Ye are the light of the world... Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.

ambassadorPoints.title: 1. Share the Gospel Intentionally Online
points: Social media should not only be a place where believers consume content but where they contribute to God's mission.
Practical ways include:
• Sharing Bible verses with thoughtful reflections rather than posting them without context.
• Posting testimonies of God's faithfulness.
• Sharing sermon clips or devotionals that encourage others.
• Inviting friends to church events or Bible studies through digital platforms.
Remember: Not every post has to preach, but every post should reflect Christ-like character.
“...Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature.” — Mark 16:15
Today, "all the world" includes digital spaces.

ambassadorPoints.title: 2. Create God-Honoring Content
points: The internet needs more creators than critics.
Believers gifted in various fields can create:
• Podcasts
• Christian blogs
• Educational videos
• Bible study resources
• Music
• Animations
• Graphic designs
• Short inspirational videos
• Christian mobile applications
God uses different gifts to reach different people.

ambassadorPoints.title: 3. Build Technology that Serves God's Purposes
points: Not everyone is called to preach from a pulpit, but some are called to build tools that advance ministry.
Examples include:
• Bible reading apps
• Church management systems
• Online giving platforms
• Christian educational websites
• Prayer request platforms
• Gospel games for children
• Translation tools for unreached languages
• AI tools that help people study Scripture responsibly
As developers, designers, engineers, and innovators, believers can view their work as ministry.
God filled Bezalel with wisdom and skill to build for His glory. Likewise, technical skills can be dedicated to God's work today. — Exodus 31:1–5

ambassadorPoints.title: 4. Practice Digital Discipleship
points: Jesus commanded us to make disciples, not merely gain followers.
Technology enables us to:
• Host virtual Bible studies.
• Mentor younger believers through video calls.
• Encourage others through group chats.
• Pray with people online.
• Answer sincere questions about Christianity with grace and truth.
Sometimes a simple encouraging message may be exactly what someone needs.

ambassadorPoints.title: 5. Defend Truth with Grace
points: The internet is full of misinformation, false teachings, and hostile debates.
Believers should:
• Verify information before sharing it.
• Correct error respectfully.
• Avoid spreading rumors.
• Speak truth with humility.
“Speaking the truth in love...” — Ephesians 4:15
Winning an argument is less important than reflecting Christ.

ambassadorPoints.title: 6. Support Digital Missions
points: Not everyone will become a content creator.
Some can contribute by:
• Supporting online missionaries.
• Volunteering technical skills for churches.
• Designing ministry websites.
• Editing videos for evangelistic outreaches.
• Managing church social media pages.
• Helping elderly church members access online services.
Every gift can advance God's Kingdom.

ambassadorPoints.title: 7. Model Christ-like Character Online
points: One of the greatest evangelistic tools is a transformed life.
Ask yourself before posting:
• Is it true?
• Is it helpful?
• Is it loving?
• Does it glorify Christ?
• Would I be comfortable if Jesus read this post with me?
Our digital footprints should point people toward Christ rather than away from Him.

lines: This generation does not need believers who escape technology,
Are spiritually rooted, Digitally wise, God-centered in identity
We are not called to be offline saints, but anchored disciples.
The future of faith is not anti-technology—it is Christ-centered people navigating technology without losing their soul.
slides.closingVerse: “What shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his soul?
slides.meta:
FAITH IN A DIGITAL AGE


Staying God-Centered in a Tech-Driven World
2026

title: Monetization & Skill Positioning
description: Packaging Your Skills, Introduction to Freelancing, Digital Safety & Portfolio Presentation

slides.title: MONETIZATION & SKILL POSITIONING
slides.subtitle: Packaging Your Skills, Introduction to Freelancing, Digital Safety & Portfolio Presentation
slides.facilitatorRole: COO & Lead Software Engineer, Blink Labs
slides.targetAudience: Students, young professionals, creatives, developers, freelancers, and digital talent across Nigeria and Africa
slides.meta:
MONETIZATION & SKILL POSITIONING
Packaging Your Skills, Introduction to Freelancing, Digital Safety & Portfolio Presentation

slides.title: YOUR SKILL HAS VALUE—BUT VALUE ALONE DOES NOT GUARANTEE INCOME
slides.theme: You must know how to position, package, present, protect, and sell that value.
points: A lot of talented people across Nigeria and Africa have valuable skills.
The problem is not always a lack of talent.
People often do not know:
• What exactly they are selling
• Who they are selling it to
• How to communicate the value of what they do
• How to price or package their work
• How to present proof that they can actually deliver
• How to protect themselves in the digital economy
slides.keyPoint: A skill is not automatically a business.

slides.title: SKILL VS. POSITIONING

comparison.label: Designer A
comparison.content: "I am a graphic designer. I can design flyers, logos, banners, anything."

comparison.label: Designer B
comparison.content: "I help small businesses create professional social media designs that make their brand look credible and attract more customers."

slides.lesson: Both may have the same technical skill. But the second person has positioned their skill around a specific result for a specific audience.

slides.title: HOW YOU WANT PEOPLE TO UNDERSTAND YOUR SKILL
slides.formula: I help [TARGET AUDIENCE] achieve [RESULT] using [YOUR SKILL].

examples.statement: I help startups build fast and reliable web applications using modern technologies.
I help businesses create professional visual identities that improve brand perception.
I help small businesses maintain a consistent social media presence and connect with customers online.
I help creators transform raw footage into engaging content optimized for social media.
I help busy entrepreneurs organize administrative tasks so they can focus on growing their business.

slides.title: CLARITY ATTRACTS OPPORTUNITY
points: One major mistake beginners make is saying: "I can do everything."
You may have multiple skills, but your communication should be clear.
If your profile lists too many specializations, potential clients may ask: "What exactly is this person best at?"
You do not necessarily need to have only one skill.
But you need to communicate your main professional value clearly.

slides.title: TURNING ABILITIES INTO CLEAR OFFERS

comparison.label: Offer
comparison.content: I will edit 10 short-form videos per month for your business, including captions, transitions, basic motion graphics, and social-media-ready exports.

slides.lesson: People should not have to guess what you do, what they will receive, how long it takes, or what problem it solves.

slides.eyebrow: THE 5 PARTS OF A GOOD SERVICE PACKAGE
slides.title: STRUCTURE YOUR OFFER CLEARLY

parts.title: The Timeline
parts.desc: When will the work be delivered?

parts.title: The Scope
parts.desc: What is included and what is not included?

parts.title: The Price
parts.desc: Project-based, hourly, weekly, monthly, or packages

slides.title: DON'T JUST SELL YOUR TIME
slides.lesson: For example, a business owner may not care how many hours you spent designing something. They may care about:
points: Whether it looks professional
Whether it represents their brand
Whether it helps them communicate better
Whether you deliver on time
Whether you are reliable
slides.quote: Do not just sell your time. Learn to communicate your value.

slides.title: OFFERING YOUR SKILLS INDEPENDENTLY
slides.definition: Freelancing means offering your skills and services independently to clients.

channels.title: 1. Freelance Platforms
points: Platforms where clients post jobs and freelancers apply or create service listings
Advantage: Access to a wider market
Challenge: Competition with professionals globally
Your profile, portfolio, communication, reviews, and proposal quality affect your chances

channels.title: 2. Direct Clients
points: Clients you find yourself
Examples: A business on Instagram, a startup founder on LinkedIn, a local company, a church or organization, someone referred by a previous client
Requires networking and communication

channels.title: 3. Referrals
points: One of the most powerful sources of work
A happy client can tell another person: "This person did a good job for me."
That is why professionalism matters
Sometimes your next client is connected to your previous client

mistakes.title: Waiting Until You Are Perfect
points: Many say: "I am still learning." Yes, keep learning. But you can also begin building.
You do not need to know everything before creating practice projects, demo projects, case studies, or sample work.

mistakes.title: Copying Everyone Else
points: Do not build your career only by asking: "What is everyone doing?"
Ask: "Where can my skills solve real problems?"

mistakes.title: Charging Without Understanding Scope
points: Before accepting a project, understand: What is required? How many deliverables? How many revisions? What is the deadline? What happens if the client adds more work?
A clear agreement can prevent many problems.

mistakes.title: Saying Yes to Everything
points: Not every project is a good project.
Learn to identify unrealistic deadlines, unclear requirements, excessive revision requests, and clients who refuse to define payment terms.

slides.title: WHERE ARE YOUR CLIENTS?
slides.question: Can they clearly understand what you do when they find you?

slides.eyebrow: THE IMPORTANCE OF YOUR DIGITAL PRESENCE
slides.title: CLARITY IS POWERFUL
questions: Can you prove that you can do it?

examples.label: Bad Profile
examples.note: It may sound interesting, but it does not tell a client what you actually offer.

examples.label: Better Profile
examples.content: "Frontend Developer | Building fast and responsive web applications for startups and businesses."

examples.label: Better Profile
examples.content: "Video Editor | Helping brands and creators produce engaging short-form content."

examples.label: Instead of
examples.content: "I can do anything you want, sir. Please give me the job."

examples.label: Try
examples.content: "Thank you for reaching out. Based on your requirements, I can help with [specific service]. The project would include [deliverables]. Before we proceed, I would like to confirm the timeline and scope."

slides.title: PROTECT YOURSELF IN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY
slides.intro: Your digital career can be affected by account hacking, scams, fake clients, phishing links, payment fraud, identity theft, malware, and social engineering.

rules.title: PROTECT YOUR ACCOUNTS
points: Use strong passwords
Different passwords for important accounts
A reputable password manager where possible
Two-factor authentication
Do not use the same password everywhere

rules.title: WATCH OUT FOR PHISHING
points: A scammer may send a message claiming you received a payment or your account will be suspended
Always check: The sender, the website address, whether the request makes sense
Do not enter passwords or sensitive information on suspicious websites

rules.title: BE CAREFUL WITH CLIENT FILES
points: Files can contain malware
Be cautious with unknown executable files, suspicious ZIP files, unexpected attachments, and fake software installers

rules.title: DON'T SHARE SENSITIVE INFORMATION CARELESSLY
points: Be careful with passwords, one-time verification codes, recovery phrases, private keys, banking credentials, and government identification documents
No legitimate person needs your password or one-time verification code to send you money

rules.title: USE CLEAR PAYMENT ARRANGEMENTS
points: Before beginning major work, clarify: Total project cost, payment structure, deposit requirements, payment milestones, final delivery terms
For certain projects, consider upfront deposits, milestone payments, or platform escrow where available and appropriate

slides.keyPrinciple: Urgency is often used to make people stop thinking.

slides.title: SHOW YOUR WORK PROFESSIONALLY
slides.definition: A portfolio is evidence. It answers the question: "Can you actually do what you claim to do?"
slides.note: The most important thing is not the platform. It is the presentation.

slides.eyebrow: WHAT SHOULD A GOOD PORTFOLIO SHOW?
slides.title: FOUR KEY ELEMENTS

elements.title: Who You Are
elements.desc: A short introduction. Example: "I am a frontend developer focused on building responsive and user-friendly web applications."

elements.title: What You Do
elements.desc: Clearly list your services or areas of expertise.

elements.title: Your Best Work
elements.desc: Do not upload everything you have ever done. Show your strongest and most relevant work.

elements.title: Context
elements.desc: Explain: What was the problem? What was your role? What tools did you use? What was the solution? What was the outcome?

slides.title: FOR A SOFTWARE DEVELOPER

example.title: E-Commerce Platform
example.problem: The business needed a simple way for customers to browse products and place orders.
example.outcome: Created a functional demo showing the complete customer journey.

slides.note: This gives the viewer more confidence in your ability.

slides.eyebrow: WHAT IF YOU DON'T HAVE CLIENT WORK?
slides.title: OPTIONS FOR BEGINNERS

options.title: 1. Personal Projects
options.desc: Build something based on your interests.

options.title: 2. Redesign Projects
options.desc: Take an existing concept and redesign it for practice. Clearly indicate that it is a concept or practice project if it was not commissioned.

options.title: 3. Volunteer Work
options.desc: Where appropriate, work with student organizations, communities, NGOs, churches, or small businesses. But do not allow "free work" to become permanent exploitation.

options.title: 4. Case Studies
options.desc: Show how you would solve a particular problem.

slides.title: AVOID THESE ERRORS
mistakes: Too Much Work — More work does not always mean a better portfolio.
No Explanation — Don't just dump images and screenshots.
Poor Organization — Make it easy for people to navigate.
Fake Claims — Never claim you worked for a company when you did not. Trust takes time to build and seconds to destroy.

days.title: Identify Your Main Skill
days.task: Write down: What you can do, What you enjoy doing, What problems you can solve

days.title: Choose an Audience
days.task: Who needs this skill? Examples: Businesses, Startups, Creators, Organizations

days.title: Package One Service
days.task: Define: Deliverables, Timeline, Scope, Revisions, Pricing approach

days.title: Create or Improve One Portfolio Project
Improve Your Online Presence
days.task: Update: LinkedIn, Portfolio, Professional bio, Contact information

days.title: Reach Out
days.task: Take action. Apply for an opportunity, Contact a potential client professionally, Join a professional community, Publish your work, Ask for feedback

takeaways.title: 1. Your Skill Is Only the Beginning
takeaways.desc: Having a skill is important. Knowing how to communicate its value is equally important.

takeaways.title: 2. Clarity Attracts Opportunity
takeaways.desc: People should understand: What you do, Who you help, What result you provide

takeaways.title: 3. Package Your Work
takeaways.desc: Turn "I am good at this" into "This is the specific service I offer, this is what you receive, and this is the problem it solves."

takeaways.title: 4. Build Proof
takeaways.desc: Do not wait for a perfect opportunity before building a portfolio. Create. Document. Publish. Improve.

takeaways.title: 5. Protect Yourself
takeaways.desc: The digital economy creates opportunities, but it also creates risks. Protect: Your accounts, Your identity, Your devices, Your finances, Your professional reputation

takeaways.title: 6. Start Before You Feel Completely Ready
takeaways.desc: Your first portfolio may not be perfect. Your first proposal may not be perfect. Your first client conversation may not be perfect. But: You cannot improve from opportunities you never pursue.

slides.title: YOUR SKILL CAN BECOME INCOME
lines: Nigeria does not lack skilled young people.
What we often need is better positioning, better execution, stronger proof of work, professional communication, and the confidence to participate in the global digital economy.
Your location should not limit your ambition.
Your current level should not stop your growth.
Start with what you know, improve continuously, package your value, protect yourself, and let your work speak.
The goal is not just to have a skill.
The goal is to build a skill that solves problems, create proof that you can deliver, and position yourself where opportunities can find you.
But first, you must learn how to position your value.
